decision: Separate FA3 logical secret-backend admission from system-wide Secret Service bus-name interoperability. Prefer org.freedesktop.secrets. On the KDE Plasma Tier-1 reference desktop only, a canonical provider-specific bus alias may satisfy FA3 SECRET_BACKEND when exact XML D-Bus introspection proves org.freedesktop.Secret.Service on /org/freedesktop/secrets. Such an alias never proves the standard bus name and never claims system-wide Secret Service interoperability.
rationale: FA3-DESKTOP-BASE-001 requires the logical SECRET_BACKEND capability through SECRET_SERVICE_OR_FA3_VAULT rather than a provider-specific desktop API.
KDE's 2026 KWallet architecture separates the KWallet compatibility proxy from ksecretd, which implements the Secret Service API and may expose a provider-specific compatibility bus name.
Requiring the global org.freedesktop.secrets name for FA3's own adapter would conflate system-wide client interoperability with the narrower logical secret-backend capability.
Name-only acceptance is forbidden; exact interface proof and reference-profile scoping remain fail-closed.
